roadmap.goal: Slice 04 (value, US-05, ADO #5549): the "PBC Over Time" widget toggles across ALL SIX process-behaviour metric families instead of Throughput alone, each reading its own persisted NPL daily series. Five members are APPENDED to `ProcessBehaviorMetricType` -> the recorder's per-scope `readers` array records every family the scope can read (5 for a team, 6 for a portfolio — Feature Size is portfolio-only because there is no team-side read method, D8) -> a new ready-but-zero honesty gate stops a flat zero band the owner never had from being persisted (US-05 AC4 / D6) -> the frontend's metric-type list becomes scope-aware and the toggle grows human-readable labels while keeping the shipped `pbc-metric-<lowercased>` locator convention. Closes milestone-4 Scenarios 13, 14 and 15. NO new endpoint, NO controller change, NO new table, NO EF migration, NO demo-backfill extension.
roadmap.overview: Single phase (04), 5 steps in dependency order. Backbone: 04-01 the ready-but-zero honesty gate FIRST, as a self-contained fix on the shipped single-family recorder, so the five new families inherit a correct gate instead of shipping five ways to persist a zero band and fixing it after -> 04-02 append the five enum members and lift the `readers` array into the two per-scope `HandleAsync` methods -> 04-03 the slice-04 acceptance fixture pair at the read port (where the per-family dated triple IS drivable) plus the `CycleTime`-sentinel repair in the shipped slice-03 fixture -> 04-04 the frontend scope-aware metric list, the `ownerType` prop and the labelled toggle -> 04-05 E2E POM/spec + the docs claims that go stale, then the full local gate sweep. RED = RED-by-skip (project convention, DISTILL [REF] RED Mechanism): NUnit ATs and Playwright specs are authored with `[Ignore("pending — DELIVER (epic-5427 slice-04)")]` / `test.skip` alongside the minimal type changes so `main` always compiles and stays green; each step un-ignores only its own scenarios. Mostly data + configuration over the shell slice 03 built — the two genuine changes are the honesty gate (backend behaviour, app-wide for the recorder) and the scope-aware toggle (frontend structure).

validation.notes: Six facts were established by reading the shipped code before this roadmap was written and MUST NOT be re-litigated: (1) `ProcessBehaviorMetricType` holds exactly one member, `Throughput`, and its own XML doc states the persistence contract — persisted as the integer ordinal, APPEND ONLY. (2) All five team-side and all six portfolio-side `Get*ProcessBehaviourChart(owner, DateTime, DateTime)` read methods already exist — nothing new is computed this slice. (3) `ProcessBehaviorRecordingHandler` already carries the per-type seam slice-03 built for this slice: a `readers` array plus a per-type inner try/catch in `RecordMetricType`. (4) Both controllers' `GetProcessBehaviorOverTime` are already generic over the enum and guarded by `Enum.IsDefined(type)` -> 400 (`TeamMetricsController.cs:537` and the `PortfolioMetricsController` twin) — NO controller change is needed, and step 04-03 verifies that empirically rather than assuming it. (5) `IProcessBehaviorSeriesQuery` / `ProcessBehaviorSnapshotRepository.GetSeries` already filter on `MetricType`, so per-family isolation is already implemented. (6) No EF migration: appending enum members changes no schema — `ProcessBehaviorSnapshot.MetricType` is already an int column. Two maintainer decisions of 2026-07-26 are binding: the ready-but-zero gate goes in `RecordMetricType`, NOT in the chart builders; and `DemoPercentilesBackfillHandler` is NOT extended, which is why the per-family dated-triple assertion lives at the read port and not in the E2E.

open_questions_resolved.enum_growth_direction: RESOLVED by the enum's own contract: APPEND `WorkItemAge, Wip, CycleTime, Arrivals, FeatureSize` after `Throughput`, giving ordinals Throughput=0, WorkItemAge=1, Wip=2, CycleTime=3, Arrivals=4, FeatureSize=5. Member NAMES follow the DESIGN driving-ports vocabulary (feature-delta L300: `{Throughput|WorkItemAge|Wip|CycleTime|Arrivals|FeatureSize}`), not the read-method names — the WorkItemAge family reads `GetTotalWorkItemAgeProcessBehaviourChart`, and that asymmetry is deliberate and pre-decided. Alphabetising or grouping members is FORBIDDEN: the ordinal is the persisted value and Throughput=0 is already on disk in every shipped instance.
open_questions_resolved.readers_array_lift: RESOLVED — and this is the one place the "extend the array, do not restructure the handler" instruction needs a precise reading. The array is currently built INSIDE `RecordAsync`, which receives a single `Func<DateTime,DateTime,ProcessBehaviourChart>`. A team can read five families and a portfolio six, so the array cannot stay inside a scope-agnostic method. The minimal change is to move the array construction UP into each `HandleAsync` (each scope already holds its own strongly-typed service and owner entity) and have `RecordAsync` take `(ProcessBehaviorMetricType, Func<DateTime,DateTime,ProcessBehaviourChart>)[] readers` in place of the single Func. `RecordAsync`'s param count stays 5; `RecordMetricType`, its inner try/catch, `UpsertSnapshot`, `LookbackDaysFor` and the `finally`-block invalidation are untouched. That is an extension of the seam, not a restructure — but it IS more than adding rows to a literal, so it is called out rather than smuggled in.
open_questions_resolved.zero_gate_placement: RESOLVED (maintainer decision 2026-07-26): the gate goes in `ProcessBehaviorRecordingHandler.RecordMetricType`, as `if (chart.Average == 0 && chart.UpperNaturalProcessLimit == 0) { return; }` alongside the existing `Status != Ready` guard. It must NOT go in the three chart builders: making them report `InsufficientData` would change the six SHIPPED point-in-time PBC widgets app-wide, far outside this slice. The gate deliberately does NOT test `Lnpl == 0` — XmRCalculator.cs:46 clamps a negative LNPL to zero for zero-bounded data, so a legitimate, well-populated process routinely has `Lnpl == 0`, and including it in the predicate would silently stop recording real data.
open_questions_resolved.zero_gate_reachability: RESOLVED by reading the code, not by argument: all three builders set `Status = BaselineStatus.Ready` unconditionally after `BaselineValidationService.Validate` passes (BaseMetricsService.cs:614, :676, :750), and `XmRCalculator.Calculate` returns `(0, 0, 0)` for an empty baseline (XmRCalculator.cs:17-21) and for an all-zero baseline (average 0, mrBar 0). So `Ready` + 0/0/0 is reachable today, the shipped `Status != Ready` gate does not catch it, and a flat zero band the owner never had is currently persistable. An absent row is the honest empty state (US-05 AC4 / D6).
open_questions_resolved.per_family_dated_triple_seam: RESOLVED (maintainer decision 2026-07-26 — demo backfill stays Throughput-only): milestone-4's Scenario Outline says "three dated lines are plotted for <metric_type>", which CANNOT be driven through the UI for the five new families, because on demo data they have at most the single row today's refresh recorded. That assertion is therefore routed to the read port: a NUnit `WebApplicationFactory` acceptance fixture seeds `ProcessBehaviorSnapshot` rows per family and asserts the dated triple comes back per family, plus cross-family isolation. The Playwright E2E keeps what it can honestly observe: the toggle offers the right families per scope, Feature Size is portfolio-only, Throughput still plots its dated triple, and a family with nothing recorded shows the honest D6 copy. The crafter must NOT try to force the E2E to plot a new family.
open_questions_resolved.e2e_empty_copy_owner: RESOLVED against the handoff's wording, deliberately. The honest-empty-copy assertion for a new family belongs on the FRESH, never-refreshed team on a non-demo connection (the shipped `@edge @US-04` spec's setup), NOT on the demo team. On the demo team, the refresh that `waitForBackgroundUpdates` waits for now runs the EXTENDED recorder, so each new family gets TODAY's row and the widget is not empty — the copy assertion would fail, and would fail intermittently depending on whether the family's baseline came back non-zero. The fresh team has nothing recorded for ANY family, which makes the assertion deterministic while still testing exactly the AC4 behaviour.
open_questions_resolved.feature_size_enforcement_layer: RESOLVED: D8's portfolio-only constraint is enforced at the TOGGLE (the frontend never offers Feature Size at team scope), not at the wire. `?type=FeatureSize` on the team endpoint therefore answers 200 with an empty series — `Enum.IsDefined` passes and no team row is ever recorded. Step 04-03 asserts that SHIPPED behaviour explicitly rather than leaving it unstated. Adding a scope-aware 400 guard to the team controller was considered and rejected: new code for a case no client can reach, on an endpoint whose 400s currently mean exactly one thing ("that is not a metric family"). Recorded as a decision, not skipped.
open_questions_resolved.no_controller_change: RESOLVED by reading TeamMetricsController.cs:536-553: the action's parameter is already `ProcessBehaviorMetricType`, defaulted to Throughput, guarded by `Enum.IsDefined`, and forwarded verbatim to the query port. Appending enum members makes the new families valid with zero controller edits. Step 04-03 VERIFIES this empirically by exercising every family through the untouched controllers; if any family needs a controller edit, the crafter stops and reports rather than editing silently.
open_questions_resolved.no_hook_change: RESOLVED by reading usePbcOverTime.ts: `cacheKey(metricType, startDate, endDate)` already includes the family, so six families cache and re-plot independently with no hook edit. Verify by test, do not assume. If a scope-aware reset of the selected family turns out to be needed, it belongs in the widget (which knows `ownerType`), never in the hook (which has no opinion about scope).
open_questions_resolved.toggle_label_source: RESOLVED: labels come from `useTerminology()` inside the widget, matching the vocabulary the six SIBLING point-in-time PBC widgets already use (BaseMetricsView.tsx:811-854) — Throughput / Work Item Age / Work In Progress / Cycle Time / Arrivals / Feature Size. `useTerminology()` falls back to a provider-independent default map (TerminologyContext.tsx:99-112) whose values are exactly the `.feature` file's wording, so no new test provider is needed and the `.feature` stays satisfied. Hard-coding English labels in the model file was the alternative; rejected because every other metric label in this view is terminology-driven and a hard-coded label would silently ignore a tenant's renamed terms.
open_questions_resolved.no_migration: RESOLVED: zero schema delta. Appending enum members does not change the `ProcessBehaviorSnapshot.MetricType` int column, no new property appears on any persisted model, and no index changes. The `CreateMigration` script is NOT run this slice. If the crafter's model diff shows ANY DDL, that is a signal the slice drifted out of scope — stop and report.

phases.name: PBC over time across all six process-behaviour metric families
phases.description: Append five enum members, record every family the scope can read, refuse to persist a zero band nobody had, and make the toggle scope-aware and human-readable. No new component, port, route, table or migration.

steps.name: Ready-but-zero honesty gate on the process-behaviour recorder
criteria: `ProcessBehaviorRecordingHandler.RecordMetricType` returns WITHOUT upserting when `chart.Average == 0 && chart.UpperNaturalProcessLimit == 0`, in addition to the existing `chart.Status != BaselineStatus.Ready` guard — an absent row is the honest empty state (US-05 AC4 / D6)

A test proves the case is REACHABLE rather than hypothetical: a chart with `Status = Ready` and `Average = UNPL = LNPL = 0` (what `XmRCalculator.Calculate` returns for an empty or all-zero baseline while all three builders still report `Ready`) writes NO row
A test proves a legitimate non-zero `Ready` chart still records — the shipped happy path is unchanged (regression)

A test pins the boundary the gate must NOT cross: a chart with a non-zero Average/UNPL but `Lnpl == 0` DOES record. XmRCalculator clamps a negative LNPL to zero for zero-bounded data, so a real process routinely has `Lnpl == 0`, and folding it into the predicate would stop recording real data

A test covers the same-day re-run case: when a non-zero row already exists for today and the fresh read comes back Ready-but-zero, the existing row keeps its non-zero values rather than being overwritten with zeros

The three chart builders (`BuildDailyRunChartProcessBehaviourChart`, `BuildTotalWorkItemAgeProcessBehaviourChart`, `BuildCycleTimeProcessBehaviourChart`) and `BaselineStatus` are UNTOUCHED — the six shipped point-in-time PBC widgets keep reporting `Ready` exactly as today, verified by their existing suites staying green with no edits
The gate lives in `RecordMetricType`, so every family added in 04-02 inherits it without a second gate site
`dotnet build` zero warnings; `dotnet test` green. Any slice-04 acceptance scenario authored ahead of time stays `[Ignore("pending — DELIVER (epic-5427 slice-04)")]`
steps.scenario_name: Scenario 13 precondition (US-05 AC4 / D6) — a Ready-but-zero natural-process band is not persisted, so an absent row stays the honest empty state
steps.implementation_notes: This is the slice's one genuine behaviour change and it gets its own commit so it is independently reviewable and revertible — it changes recording semantics for the SHIPPED Throughput family too, not only for the new ones. It goes FIRST so the five families added in 04-02 inherit a correct gate, instead of shipping five ways to persist a zero band and fixing it afterwards. Extend the existing `ReadyChart(unpl, average, lnpl)` helper rather than adding a parallel factory. ci-learnings to pre-apply: NUnit4002 — `Is.Zero`, never `Is.EqualTo(0)`; `Is.Default`, never `Is.EqualTo(default(X))`; NUnit2056 — `using (Assert.EnterMultipleScope())`, never `Assert.Multiple(...)`; NUnit2046 — `Has.Count.EqualTo(N)`, never `Assert.That(x.Count, ...)`; CA1861 — hoist any inline `new[] {...}` in an assertion to a `static readonly` field; CA1859 — a NEW private helper that only builds/consumes `List<T>` must be typed `List<T>`, never `IReadOnlyList<T>`; S2139 — do not log-and-rethrow, the existing catch already logs and the dispatcher swallows. Mutation-dense spot: the `&&` and both `== 0` comparisons — Stryker flips `&&` to `||` and `== 0` to `!= 0`, and the four tests above are shaped so each flip is killed by a different one. After writing the gate, sabotage it (widen the predicate to `chart.Average >= 0`) and confirm red before restoring — `if (false)` does NOT work for this in C#, `TreatWarningsAsErrors` turns CS0162 unreachable-code into a build error.

steps.name: Append the five metric families and record every family the scope can read
criteria: `ProcessBehaviorMetricType` APPENDS `WorkItemAge, Wip, CycleTime, Arrivals, FeatureSize` after `Throughput`; no member is reordered or renumbered, so ordinals are Throughput=0, WorkItemAge=1, Wip=2, CycleTime=3, Arrivals=4, FeatureSize=5 and every already-persisted row keeps its meaning
A test pins each member's integer ordinal explicitly, so a future alphabetisation or insertion fails loudly at test time instead of silently re-mapping shipped snapshot rows

`HandleAsync(TeamDataRefreshed)` records FIVE families (Throughput, WorkItemAge, Wip, CycleTime, Arrivals) from `ITeamMetricsService`; `HandleAsync(PortfolioFeaturesRefreshed)` records SIX (those five plus FeatureSize) from `IPortfolioMetricsService`. The asymmetry is structural — there is no team-side Feature Size read method to call (D8, US-05 AC2)

The `readers` array construction moves from inside `RecordAsync` up into the two `HandleAsync` methods, and `RecordAsync` takes `(ProcessBehaviorMetricType, Func<DateTime,DateTime,ProcessBehaviourChart>)[] readers` in place of its single `Func`. `RecordMetricType`, its per-type inner try/catch, `UpsertSnapshot`, `LookbackDaysFor` and the `finally`-block cache invalidation are UNCHANGED

Each family's row carries its OWN `MetricType` and its OWN triple: a test asserts the recorded rows are five (team) / six (portfolio) DISTINGUISHABLE rows for the same owner and day, comparing the exact family SET, not just a row count, and not five copies of Throughput's numbers
